title: Relative curves without a separatedness assumption
statement: Let $T,X$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $x:X\to T$ a morphism. It is a relative $T$-curve if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has pure dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. No separatedness or properness is required. Empty fibres are allowed, with pure dimension interpreted vacuously on them.

source.place: Temkin, Stable modification of relative curves, §1.2 (relative curves).
